title: Frontend mid systemdesign infinite scroll feed
topic: Frontend mid systemdesign infinite scroll feed
question: Design the client-side architecture for an infinite-scroll social feed, similar to a typical timeline, that stays smooth even after the user has scrolled through thousands of posts.
idealAnswer:
Use an IntersectionObserver (or scroll-position calculation) on a sentinel element near the bottom to trigger fetching the next page, rather than listening to every scroll event, which is expensive and imprecise

Use cursor-based pagination (based on an opaque cursor or timestamp/id) rather than offset-based pagination, offsets shift and cause duplicate or skipped items if new posts are inserted while scrolling

Virtualize the rendered list (rendering only DOM nodes for posts near the viewport) so memory and rendering cost stay flat instead of growing unbounded as thousands of posts accumulate

Handle images and media lazily, loading media only as items approach the viewport, to avoid huge upfront bandwidth and memory use

Decide how to handle new content arriving at the top while the user is scrolled deep into the feed, typically buffering it behind a 'new posts' affordance rather than silently shifting content underneath the user

Plan for error and retry states per page fetch, and preserve scroll position correctly if the user navigates away and back
